To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the high temperature superconductivity in copper and iron oxides is due to a Little-Ginzburg CT-excitonic pairing of charge carriers in conducting layers of the Ginzburg HTCS-'sandwiches'.

the high critical temperature of HTSC transition is due to the Little-Ginz- burg exciton mechanism of superconductivity, when mobile charge-transfer excitons mediate the Cooper pairing of charge carriers.

high-Tc superconductivity in doped copper and iron oxides is due to the Little-Ginzberg CT-exciton pairing mechanism, which is realized in these compounds due to the formation of planar GINSBURG HTSC-'sandwicnes' (insulator-metal-insulator) within their conducting planes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of superconductivity in the new iron-based superconductor.
the mechanism of superconducting phase transition in doped copper oxide and iron-based high temperature superconductors (HTSC).
the problem of the origin of the high temperature superconductivity in cuprates and iron pnictide superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high critical temperature of the superconducting transition is reached due to the Little-Ginzberg exciton mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity in cuprates and iron pnictide superconductors.
HTSC is the Little-Ginzbug excitonic superconductivity.

the high-temperature superconductivity in cuprates is a result of the Ginzburg exciton condensation in a series of planer Ginzburg HTCS-'sandwiches' which are formed in the conducting planes of cuprates below the onset temperature of pseudogap in the normal state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Little-Ginzberg exciton mechanism of superconductivity is realized in HTSC compounds with the optimal parameters of charge transfer (CT) exciton in outer 'insulator' layers.

the Little-Ginzberg exciton mechanism of Cooper pairing of charge carriers in cuprates is realized in planar 'insulating' layers of the stripe structure, and in iron pnictides in planar'metallic' layers of the'metal-insulator-metal' sandwich structure, and that the high critical temperature of HTSC in both classes of cuprates and iron pnictide superconductors is due to the mobile CT-exciton pairing of charge carriers.
the HTSC phenomenon is a result of a synergy between the Ginzburg exciton and the Little pairing mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Little-Ginzurg exciton mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity is a general one for doped copper oxide and iron pnictide HTSC.

the Little-Ginzberg mechanism of HTSC is realized in doped cuprates and iron pnictide compounds, where the exciton mechanism of superconducting pairing is provided by the planar Ginzbug HTSC-'sandwishes' in conducting planes.

the high critical temperature in HTSC and new iron-based compounds is reached because of a series of planer Ginzburg'sandwiches' of 'insulator' -'metal'-'insulator' type naturally forming in conducting layers below the onset pseudgap temperature in normal state.
